officialTitle: Olaparib for Metastatic Breast Cancer in Patients with a Germline BRCA Mutation
setting: Metastatic, no more than two previous chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Of the 302 patients who underwent randomization, 205 were assigned to receive olaparib and 97 were assigned to receive standard therapy.
design.notes: 2:1 randomisation. Comparator: single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice (capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine).

clinicalQuestion: Is olaparib monotherapy superior to physician's choice chemotherapy in germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer?

pico.population: Germline BRCA mutation, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, ≤2 previous chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease
pico.comparator: Single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice (capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine)
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by BICR. Secondary: response rate, safety

arms.label: Olaparib
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, to receive olaparib tablets (300 mg twice daily) or standard therapy with single-agent chemotherapy of the physician's choice (capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine in 21-day cycles).

arms.label: Physician's choice chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine (physician's choice), 21-day cycles

publications.title: Olaparib for Metastatic Breast Cancer in Patients with a Germline BRCA Mutation.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Median progression-free survival was significantly longer in the olaparib group than in the standard-therapy group (7.0 months vs. 4.2 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval, 0.43 to 0.80; P<0.001).
The response rate was 59.9% in the olaparib group and 28.8% in the standard-therapy group.

safety.sourceQuote: The rate of grade 3 or higher adverse events was 36.6% in the olaparib group and 50.5% in the standard-therapy group, and the rate of treatment discontinuation due to toxic effects was 4.9% and 7.7%, respectively.

safety.description: Treatment discontinuation due to toxic effects
safety.sourceQuote: The rate of grade 3 or higher adverse events was 36.6% in the olaparib group and 50.5% in the standard-therapy group, and the rate of treatment discontinuation due to toxic effects was 4.9% and 7.7%, respectively.

strengths: First randomised phase III trial of a PARP inhibitor in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic breast cancer
PFS by blinded independent central review
limitations: OS not reported in the primary publication

clinicalImplications.text: Established olaparib as an option for germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, making germline BRCA testing relevant to treatment selection in metastatic disease.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Germline BRCA testing in HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer unlocks an oral, chemotherapy-free option with fewer grade ≥3 events than chemotherapy.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 28578601. Final OS analysis not ingested.
